artist.biography: Simone Decker was born in Esch-sur-Alzette in 1968, an industrial city in southern Luxembourg shaped by steel production and marked by cultural and linguistic intersections. From 1988 to 1993, she studied at the École des Arts Décoratifs in Strasbourg, where she developed a multidisciplinary approach combining sculpture, installation, photography, and spatial intervention.

prize.description: The Lëtzebuerger Konschtpräis is the biennial art award, established in 2022 by Luxembourg’s Ministry for Culture. The prize includes €10,000 and honours an artist for their work and ongoing commitment to Luxembourg’s art scene. The artist must be Luxembourgish, live in Luxembourg or have a strong connection with the country. After Berthe Lutgen received the prize in 2022 and Marc-Henri Reckinger in 2024, a professional jury selected Simone Decker as the 2026 laureate.

presentation.heading: PRESENTATION
presentation.intro: This presentation traces Simone Decker's artistic journey from one of her earliest exhibitions at the Nationalmusée um Fëschmaart in 1994 to the present day. Thirty-two years later, she was awarded the Lëtzebuerger Konschtpräis by the Ministry of Culture, recognising her remarkable contribution to contemporary art, both in Luxembourg and internationally. To mark this occasion, the museum’s Lëtzebuerger Konschtarchiv presents an overview of her work across three decades.
presentation.practice: Simone Decker (born 1968 in Luxembourg) invites us to see familiar places in unexpected ways. Like opening a curtain, her work encourages us to look beyond the obvious. Through her photography and interventions in public space, she uses humour, surprise and subtle shifts in perspective to question how we look at the world around us. Above all, architecture and urban spaces become starting points for exploration and (re)discovery.
presentation.discovery: Discovery lies at the heart of Decker's practice. Keep an eye out for models, prototypes and fragments of the artist’s works displayed throughout the museum’s permanent exhibition.
